_how_to_edit: The story page, replay map and home hero read this file on every load. Edit it, run `node groundstop/src/build.js`, commit and push to main; no Squarespace edit is needed. Times are hours on an Eastern clock on Nov. 13, 2026 (17.5 = 5:30 p.m.; values past 24 mean Nov. 14). Set lift to null while the stop is in effect.
headline_status: The FAA lifted the ground stop at about 8:10 p.m. Eastern, after more than four hours
cause: Telecommunications outage at air traffic control
moments: A Friday afternoon, with flights departing on schedule across the country.
About 3:10 p.m.
Flights bound for Chicago O’Hare are stopped over communications problems, and Midway follows three minutes later.
Nationwide ground stop. More than 3,100 flights already in the air are allowed to continue to their destinations.
The transportation secretary says a communication issue is affecting air route traffic control centers.
The FAA advisory now runs to 11:30 p.m. Eastern, and no end time is confirmed.
About 5:15 p.m.
The FAA says a temporary telecommunications outage caused the stop, and officials say they see no sign of an attack.
About 6:00 p.m.
The FAA says the stop remains in effect and that flights will be released as each en route center recovers.
Fox Weather counts 598 commercial flights still in the air, down from more than 3,100 when the stop began.
About 7:10 p.m.
An airline source tells CNN that major airlines could shut down operations for the rest of the night.
FlightAware counts 5,117 cancellations and 9,814 delays, and JetBlue and United call off most of their remaining Friday flights.
About 8:10 p.m.
The FAA says the nationwide ground stop is over, about 4 hours and 15 minutes after it began.
facts: Eastern start time, the only one of the three stops to begin after noon
flights in the air when the stop began, allowed to finish their trips
approximate length of the stop, against about 90 minutes in 2023, with 5,117 flights canceled by 8 p.m. Eastern
unknown: What is not known. The FAA lifted the stop at about 8:10 p.m. Eastern, according to ABC News, and has not said publicly what caused the telecommunications outage. An airline source told CNN that the FAA traced the problem to network routers and that it is believed to have started at Chicago Midway before spreading nationwide. The lift time shown here is approximate, taken from the time ABC reported the FAA's announcement. Three days earlier, on Nov. 10, the agency expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. No official has connected the tool to the stop, and no reporting so far shows a link.
status_html: The FAA lifted the stop at about 8:10 p.m. Eastern on Friday, roughly 4 hours and 15 minutes after it began, according to ABC News. Flying will take longer to recover than the stop took to end, because JetBlue canceled all of its remaining Friday flights except Europe-bound departures from New York and Boston, United said it would cancel most of its remaining flights for the night, and Air Canada canceled the rest of its Friday flights to and from the United States. FlightAware had counted 5,117 cancellations and 9,814 delays by 8 p.m., according to CNN, which is about twice the 2,500 cancellations counted at 6:30 p.m. More than 700 Saturday flights were already canceled by 7:45 p.m., and the data firm Cirium estimated that 1.5 million people were stranded.
compare_html: Friday's stop lasted about 255 minutes, close to three times the roughly 90 minutes of 2023, and it began late on a Friday afternoon where the 2023 stop began early on a Wednesday, which left airlines almost none of the day to recover. The 5,117 cancellations counted by 8 p.m. were nearly four times the 1,300-plus logged for the whole day in 2023, while the 9,814 delays were about level with that day's roughly 10,000. Cirium counted 26,284 flights scheduled to depart the United States on Friday and said more than 15% were canceled or never took off, and at least 827 flights were diverted, 670 of them back to the airport they left. The effects reach into Saturday: the Big 12 told CNN it is evaluating changes to its football schedule because teams could not travel.
notknown_html:
The FAA has not said publicly what caused the telecommunications outage. An airline source told CNN that the FAA told airlines the outages resulted from a problem with network routers, and that the problem is believed to have started at Chicago Midway and spread nationwide. CBS News reported that the affected system is operated by the contractor L3Harris, which had not responded to its request for comment. The FAA has confirmed neither account, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin were due to brief reporters at the White House on Friday night.

Mullin said there was no indication of a threat to the country, and the FAA said it does not believe the outage was a cyberattack. A senior security source told CNN late Friday that the FBI, the Department of Homeland Security and the National Security Agency had found no sign of an attack and that the search of the aviation system's network connections would continue for days.

Three days before the stop, on Nov. 10, the FAA expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. Mullin said the administration is examining that rollout, according to Fox News, and no official has connected the tool to the stop or reported a link so far.

This story reflects what was known at 8:30 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, 2026. The lift time is approximate, and we will update it, the cause and the final delay counts as the FAA and flight trackers report them.
